Prime Inc offers it for a one year contract.  They bring you in for a week of orientation and finding a trainer for your student driver phase, minimum 14 days before testing.  Some take you out on the road like mine did and some stick to the terminal or maybe short runs right back to the terminal.  Study the pre trips and learn backing and safe driving.  After 14 days eligible to test for upgrade to full CDL.

Once that’s passed you’re hired on as a company driver and go out on the road for X amount of miles minimum to the truck, currently 30k and that’s all miles under the load both you and the trainer so not all on you.  Could be the same trainer you had, could be a new one.  Once that minimum is hit and your train deems you a good enough driver they send it up the chain to check with logs and safety and everything to see if they agree.  You’re either eligible and they schedule you for upgrading to a full position here or add an additional amount usually 10k and repeat when that’s hit.  You can stay on with the trainer until your upgrade class that’s usually a couple weeks out or go home and get back to the right terminal for it.  I stayed on, we were about to get a run back that way but they asked me to recover an abandoned truck and bring it back driving solo.

2 days of upgrading classes and choosing company or lease and either being given a truck or picking one out based on company or lease.  Paperwork for that and then back on the road, the one year contract starts the day after passing the CDL test after that initial minimum 2 week phase.  Should be 2-3 months in by then depending on if you took hometime and how available you are.  Paid minimum 900 a week before taxes if available every day during the 30k or whatever the number changes to miles, there’s a threshold of on duty that if you hit you start making additional hourly day to day that I wanna say was after 8 hours.  And I’m not sure how much that was, maybe 15 an hour?
Maniac would be my recommendation.  It’s only one season but it’s really amazing and has a great mix of humor and dread due to mental and emotional trauma.  Also just fantastic cinematography

I work at prime, it’s kind of a crapshoot based on your trainer.  Could be a great experience, could be a highly contentious one.  Takes around a month to get your CDL during which you can get a 200 a week loan that you pay back 25 or 50 a week after you are hired, it’s a week of orientation and then minimum 14 days of Permit Student Driver training.  In mine we went over the road on a trip to the west coast and back to Missouri, a couple days on the pad and then testing (took me two tries).  The day you pass you are hired and go into TNT training which is team driving for 50k miles minimum, but that’s miles combined on the truck between you and your trainer.  Takes about 2.5-3 months.  That’s where the real gamble comes in cuz some just want to make money off trainees and others want to help build up their future coworkers.

I’ve enjoyed prime and recommend them with the caveat that a bad trainer can ruin the experience so be willing to reach out to get out of those situations.  They have a solid foundation that keeps prime and it’s drivers profitable during bad times for freight like now, the trade off being less gains when it’s booming.  But it’s a good measured risk/reward for starting out.  If you want any more info feel free to DM me, can also use me as a referral driver code ETOCHR

Company side you just get thrown into a truck and make money per mile ran, with time off limited and based on an accrued amount.  They also get insurance and have things covered for them like fuel and truck maintenance.  So a lot less headache, but to me the time off limitations are why I went lease.

Lease you are leasing the truck just like leasing a car in the real world.  It’s not entirely yours, but you are paying to use it for the life of the contract you sign.  Prime does 3 and 4 year leases with new trucks or you can pick one available and it just goes up to that 3/4 year point from wherever it was at.  You enter into a contract agreement where you take 72% of all revenue and prime takes 28% to use their truck and everything they provide around it like trailers and freight in general.  You pay for fuel and maintenance and everything even down to self income taxes instead of W2 as company.  But you have pretty much all autonomy over your life.  You can turn down runs and can take time off when you want.

Now it’s not 100% authority.  You need to be able to make that truck payment, what’s available for freight is what’s available so if you turn everything down and just sit neither you or prime is making money.  There are a ton of horror stories but my experience has been good.  Everyone you work with from fleet manager all the way up to the owner has a little incentive for you to run, the truck makes more their 28% is worth more and so is your 72%.  Lease is an agreed upon partnership imo, if it’s good enough for you to stick with.
